transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your valuable time today. 

Well, um, I suppose what made me come in is just... it's probably a silly thing to worry about, but my eating has gotten all turned around lately. I don't really know why, but some days I just completely forget to have lunch. And then other days, I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, but I just stand at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets. I know I shouldn't be having all those sweets at my age, and I really am trying to be better about it, I promise. It's just strange because nothing even tastes right anyway. 

I hope that's an okay reason to be here. Does that make sense?
Aside from changes in your eating, how has your mood been feeling lately?

Oh, well... I really hate to complain, doctor. I know I have so much to be thankful for, and I don't want to sound ungrateful. But, um, I suppose I have been feeling just a little... down, lately. 

It's mostly in the mornings, I think. I'll wake up and just have this very heavy, low feeling. It's almost like all the color has just gone right out of the day, and I haven't even gotten out of bed or dressed yet. I try my best to shake it off, I really do, because I know I should just put a smile on and get on with things. 

I hope I'm not sounding too gloomy... do you think that's just a normal part of getting older, feeling like that?
About how long have you been noticing this heavy, low feeling in the mornings?

Oh, goodness, let me think... I really didn't want to make a fuss about it, because I kept telling myself it would just pass on its own, you know? I didn't want to be a bother to anyone or seem like a complainer. 

But, um, if I really look back... I suppose this low, sort of colorless stretch has been with me for about... maybe a year and two months? Give or take a little bit. I know I probably should have spoken up sooner, and I'm so sorry if I let it go on too long before coming in to see you. I hope you aren't disappointed in me for waiting. Is that a terribly long time to be feeling this way, doctor?
Along with that low feeling, have you also been dealing with feelings of nervousness, worry, or anxiety?

Oh, no, doctor, I don't think so. I really try my best not to be a worrywart, you know? I know everyone has their own troubles, so I try very hard not to sit around fretting or getting all worked up over things. 

So, um, no, I wouldn't say I feel nervous or anxious... just that heavy, low feeling we were just talking about. I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope it's alright that I don't have that to report. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and being helpful.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with core symptoms of a major depressive episode, including persistent depressed mood, prominent anhedonia, appetite/eating changes, concentration difficulties, excessive guilt, and passive suicidal ideation (wishing not to wake up). Dysthymia (F34.1) was excluded due to the duration being under 2 years, and recurrent depressive disorder (F33) was excluded as this is her first lifetime episode.
